comparison: Both evaluate the core theoretical framework (C21-C25, C71). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED as internally consistent and logically coherent. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, acknowledging it's 'impressive' but expressing fundamental concerns about the crucial assumption that grid cells encode non-spatial attributes constant in space, calling it 'mere speculation' with conceptual tensions.

Both address toroidal structure claims (C35, C72-C73, C103). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting the prediction matches empirical findings and appropriately hedges novelty claims. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, suggesting the novelty claim is overstated and should acknowledge prior models more clearly (McNaughton et al., 2006; Guanella et al., 2007).

Both evaluate predictions about non-grid responses in complex environments (C85-C88). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting predictions follow from core assumptions with empirical support from Diehl et al., 2017. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, finding the points 'fair' but expressing 'theoretical disagreements' about whether grid-like coding is truly a special case.

Both address grid-like responses in non-spatial domains (C59-C62). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as logically consistent with model assumptions, though noting it's post-hoc explanation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging the model addresses these phenomena and agreeing that 'grid-like and spatial coding are a special case.'

Both evaluate neural adaptation assumptions (C38, C77-C78). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as biologically plausible with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting concern about consistency: 'habituation happens, but then spatial cell responses are supposed to be still strong after many visits,' questioning the assumption's coherence.

Both address LEC/mEC functional distinctions (C17-C19, C89-C90). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting accurate literature summary with appropriate nuance. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating 'lateral entorhinal cortex is largely ignored' and expressing confusion about why grid cells would encode attributes typically associated with LEC.

Both evaluate explanations of empirical findings (C39, C41, C53-C55). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with appropriate citations and consistent mechanisms. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging the theory 'accounts for many experimental results' without specifically challenging these explanations.

Both address grid module organization and spacing ratios (C46-C51). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting discrepancy between predicted √3 and observed √2 spacing ratio. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging the model 'tightly integrating data' and 'accounts for many experimental results' without challenging these specific features.

Both evaluate model architecture assumptions. OpenEval (C28-C31, C91-C100) rates SUPPORTED as clearly specified with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers (C28, C31-C33, C74-C75) rate UNCERTAIN, raising significant concern that 'use of border cells as main source of spatial information is not well supported' and noting border cells are a small population.

Overlapping evaluation of learning mechanisms. OpenEval (C28-C31, C91-C100) rates SUPPORTED for model architecture and learning. Peer reviewers (C91-C100) rate SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 stating the video 'makes it extremely clear how learning occurs' and no challenges to technical implementation.

Both address simulation results. OpenEval (C101-C110, C120) rates SUPPORTED with quantitative measures and internal consistency. Peer reviewers (C101-C120, broader set) also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging 'impressive computational account' and accepting simulation outcomes, though questioning underlying theoretical assumptions.

OpenEval evaluates temporal dynamics of grid formation (C111-C114) as SUPPORTED with clear quantitative results. Peer reviewers include these claims in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of simulation results (R9), acknowledging the model accounts for experimental results without challenging specific temporal dynamics.

OpenEval evaluates consolidation mechanism results (C115-C119) as SUPPORTED with clear operational definitions. Peer reviewers include these in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of simulation results, accepting the model's internal consistency without challenging these specific predictions.

Both address head direction cell predictions (C81-C82). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting testable predictions with empirical support from Bonnevie et al., 2013. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, explicitly acknowledging the prediction 'was reported by Bonnevie et al., 2013' as consistent evidence.

OpenEval evaluates predictions C81-C84 as SUPPORTED with logical derivation and some empirical support. Peer reviewers evaluate C83-C84 separately as SUPPORTED, noting the model 'generates strong predictions for future studies' without challenging these specific predictions about place cell dependence.

Both address hippocampal-entorhinal feedback (C63-C64). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, citing empirical findings that motivate model architecture. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN in broader context, noting 'discussion of continuous attractor network models is essentially absent' and that alternative frameworks explaining grid persistence are largely ignored.

Both reference grid cells during sleep (C58). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, acknowledging this as a challenge for the model. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN in broader context, noting attractor models already explain why 'grid can exist even during sleep,' suggesting the proposed model's treatment of this phenomenon is incomplete.

Partial overlap on border cell assumptions (C32-C33). OpenEval (C32-C33, C40, C52) rates SUPPORTED as logically consistent. Peer reviewers (C28, C31-C33, C74-C75) rate UNCERTAIN, challenging the foundational assumption that border cells provide main spatial information, noting they're inactive in environment centers and comprise a small population.

Minimal overlap (C40 only). OpenEval evaluates border cell alignment (C32-C33, C40, C52) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers evaluate empirical findings explanations (C39-C41, C53-C55) as SUPPORTED without specifically challenging C40, suggesting acceptance of this particular explanation.

Minimal overlap (C52 only). OpenEval evaluates multiple grid modules explanation (C32-C33, C40, C52) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers evaluate module organization (C46-C52) as SUPPORTED, acknowledging the model addresses these phenomena without challenging the multiple modules explanation.

Minimal overlap (C92-C93). OpenEval evaluates Euclidean approximation design choice (C36, C92-C93) as SUPPORTED with empirical justification. Peer reviewers evaluate learning mechanisms (C91-C100) as SUPPORTED, accepting technical implementation without specifically addressing the Euclidean approximation choice.
